knowledge-base.name: practices-commits
knowledge-base.triggers: conventional commits, commit message, git commit, commit format, feat, fix, chore, refactor, breaking change, BREAKING CHANGE, semantic versioning, changelog, commit type, commit scope, git history, squash, commit conventions
knowledge-base.overview: The Conventional Commits specification and git commit best practices. Covers commit message format, types, scopes, breaking changes, and how this connects to semantic versioning and automated changelogs.

rules.rule: The description (first line) must be in the imperative mood, lowercase after the colon, no period at end.
The first line must not exceed 72 characters.
Leave a blank line between the description and the body.
Leave a blank line between the body and each footer.
The body explains WHY the change was made, not what. The diff shows what.

examples.example: fix: prevent racing condition in order processing
feat(auth): add OAuth2 login via Google
feat!: remove deprecated payment API v1
feat(api)!: rename userId field to accountId in all responses
docs: correct example in authentication guide
chore(deps): update axios from 1.3.0 to 1.6.0

fix(auth): handle token refresh race condition
When two simultaneous requests both detect an expired token, they both try to refresh it. The second request now waits for the first to complete rather than issuing a duplicate refresh.
Refs: #4821 Reviewed-by: Jane Smith

refactor(api): replace error object shape
The `errors` array is now `error` (singular object) for consistency with RFC 7807 Problem Details.
BREAKING CHANGE: `response.errors[0]` must be changed to `response.error` in all API consumers.

type.name: feat
type.description: Introduces a new feature visible to users.

examples.example: feat: add CSV export for transaction history
feat(search): add fuzzy matching to product search

type.name: fix
type.description: Patches a bug in the codebase.

examples.example: fix: correct off-by-one error in pagination
fix(cart): prevent negative quantities on item removal

type.name: docs
type.description: Documentation changes only. No code change.

examples.example: docs: add rate limiting section to API reference
docs(readme): update local setup instructions for Windows

type.name: style
type.description: Code formatting, whitespace, missing semicolons — no logic change. Not CSS styling.

examples.example: style: apply prettier formatting to src/

type.name: refactor
type.description: Code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature. Restructuring, renaming, extracting.

examples.example: refactor(orders): extract order status logic into OrderStateMachine
refactor: replace Promise chains with async/await in payment module

type.name: test
type.description: Adding or correcting tests. No production code change.

examples.example: test: add edge case coverage for empty cart checkout
test(auth): add integration tests for token refresh flow

type.name: perf
type.semver: No version bump (but some tools treat it as PATCH)

examples.example: perf(queries): add index on orders.created_at
perf: memoize expensive category tree calculation

type.name: ci
type.description: CI/CD configuration and script changes (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, etc.).

examples.example: ci: add code coverage gate to pull request checks

type.name: build
type.description: Build system changes: webpack config, package.json scripts, Makefile, Docker.

examples.example: build: upgrade Node.js base image to 20-alpine
build(deps): update TypeScript to 5.4

type.name: chore
type.description: Catch-all for maintenance tasks that don't fit other types: dependency updates without code changes, config tweaks, generated files.

examples.example: chore: update .gitignore for VS Code workspace files
chore(deps): bump lodash from 4.17.20 to 4.17.21

type.name: revert
type.description: Reverts a previous commit. Should reference the reverted commit SHA or description.

examples.example: revert: feat(auth): add OAuth2 login via Google (refs commit abc1234)

scope.rule: Scope is optional. Use it when a commit targets a specific module, package, or subsystem.
Scope must be a noun in parentheses, lowercase: feat(auth):, fix(cart):, refactor(orders):
Be consistent with scope names across the project. Define a fixed list in CONTRIBUTING.md if helpful.
Omit scope when the change is cross-cutting or doesn't belong to a single module.

common-scopes.scope: ui — UI components (use alongside a module name for clarity)
tests — test infrastructure (not individual feature tests)

notation-1.description: Append ! after the type (and scope if present), before the colon.

examples.example: feat!: drop support for Node.js 16
fix(parser)!: change return type of parse() from string to ParseResult

notation-2.description: Include BREAKING CHANGE: in the footer, followed by a description of what changed and how to migrate.
notation-2.example:
feat(api): replace userId with accountId across all endpoints
BREAKING CHANGE: The `userId` field is removed from all API responses. Use `accountId` instead. Update all client code that reads `response.userId`.

notation-combined.description: You can use both ! and BREAKING CHANGE: footer together for clarity. If you use !, the BREAKING CHANGE footer is optional but recommended for migration guidance.

breaking-changes.semver: Breaking changes trigger a MAJOR version bump (x.0.0). This is the mechanism for coordinating major releases in automated changelog and release tools.

why-it-matters.benefit: Tools like standard-version, semantic-release, and commitizen parse conventional commits to generate CHANGELOG.md entries automatically. feat → Features section, fix → Bug Fixes section, BREAKING CHANGE → Breaking Changes section.
Automated release tools determine the next version number from commit types: feat → minor bump, fix → patch bump, BREAKING CHANGE → major bump.
git log with consistent commit types makes it fast to understand what a release contained and find when a specific change was introduced.
A well-typed commit message tells reviewers what category of change to expect before reading the diff.
Meaningful commit messages make git bisect and git blame dramatically more useful for debugging.

bad-commit-messages.bad: fix: fixed the bug where it was broken
feat: lots of changes to auth, orders, and UI plus some refactoring

commit-hygiene.rule: One commit, one logical change. Don't bundle unrelated fixes into one commit.
Commits should pass CI on their own. Never commit code that breaks the build.
Use interactive rebase (git rebase -i) to clean up WIP commits before merging, if your team's workflow allows it.
Never force-push to a shared branch (main, develop) without team consensus.
Separate refactoring commits from feature or fix commits — it makes code review and revert much easier.
